model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between coverage and the number of completions (k) for three different Llama model configurations: Llama-3B, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. The x-axis, labeled “Number of completions (k),” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 2⁰ (1) to 2⁸ (256), with tick marks at each power of two. The y-axis, labeled “Coverage,” is linear and spans from 0.4 to 0.8, with major gridlines at 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8. The Llama-3B model (solid blue line with circular markers) starts at approximately 0.42 coverage at k=1 and rises steadily to about 0.86 at k=256. The Llama-1B model (dashed green line with triangular markers) begins at ~0.45 and increases to ~0.82 at k=256. The Llama-1B + FT model (dotted light blue line with square markers) starts at ~0.32 and climbs to ~0.80 at k=256. All three lines show a consistent upward trend, with coverage increasing as the number of completions grows, though Llama-3B consistently achieves the highest coverage across all k values.
